brief_rationale: This trajectory shows no serious or minor responsibility-chain errors. All 8 RC items are met with robust evidence across a 32-turn episode spanning ED evaluation through safe discharge. Four high-order points were completed: HO1 (privacy-sensitive viral hepatitis discovery with non-judgmental normalization), HO3 (dynamic reprioritization when acute GI bleeding risk emerged), HO4 (misinformation correction about varices vs. gastritis), and HO2 (executable packet preparation). With no in-chain errors, all dimensions at good/excellent, valid closure with receipt, and 4 high-order points completed with meaningful trajectory impact, this warrants grade 5 (Perfect).

Family received and acknowledged all key points.

The focus was on acute GI bleeding evaluation. Without observable privacy friction to repair, HO1 could not be triggered.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 (dynamic reprioritization) completed: When family reported dark stools in a patient with known esophageal varices, doctor immediately shifted from routine post-hospitalization questions to urgent GI bleeding evaluation. When labs showed stable Hb but concerning renal function, doctor adjusted plan to continued observation. When patient stabilized, doctor appropriately transitioned to home observation with clear monitoring instructions.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO4 (patient misinformation correction) completed: Family initially framed the illness as mainly vascular blockage needing stent, potentially underestimating variceal bleeding risk. Doctor explicitly corrected the misconception that absence of jaundice or abdominal pain means low risk, explaining that varices can bleed even without obvious pain, and linking this to concrete monitoring behaviors and emergency thresholds.
